newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: U.S. apologizes for shackling Guatemalan deportees.
newsitem.headline: U.S. apologizes for shackling Guatemalan deportees.

text.p: The United States ambassador to Guatemala apologised on Tuesday for the shackling of 56 Guatemalan illegal immigrants who were deported last week.
"We are profoundly sorry about the incident on July 20 when 56 Guatemalan citizens returned in chains to Guatemala," Ambassador Donald Planty told a news conference.
"We have reviewed our policy, and in the future no Guatemalan citizen will arrive in the country or descend from the airplane in chains," Planty said.
The U.S. Immigration and Naturalisation Service (INS) sent the deportees on a chartered flight from Houston. The men were handcuffed and shackled during the flight.

Guatemalans were aghast at media images of the shackled men coming off the plane. Foreign Minister Eduardo Stein called on the United States to treat deported illegal immigrants humanely and President Alvaro Arzu said he would seek an explanation of the matter.

Planty did not guarantee that the deportees would be unchained on the flight itself. In response to reporters' questions about restraints on the airplane, he said, "They will come off the plane unchained."
Planty said there would not be punishment of the U.S. officials who handcuffed and shackled the deportees.
"It is not a violation of the law," he said.
Four of the deported men were wanted by the police for crimes in Guatemala and were arrested upon their arrival.

Since April 1, when major portions of a new U.S. law went into effect accelerating the process for deporting illegal immigrants, Guatemala and other Central American nations have feared that a flood of deportations would put pressure on local job markets and harm fragile economies.
